title: The ten virgins — oil in the vessel, the shut door, and I know you not (Ezekiel 36; Zechariah 4; Matthew 7)
summary:
It ain't new. Ten virgins go out to meet the bridegroom, all with lamps, and the parable turns on one thing they did not all carry:

*They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them:* (Matthew 25:3)

*But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.* (Matthew 25:4)

A lamp with no oil burns for a while on what it was lit with and then goes out. The prophets had already said what fills the vessel so the lamp keeps burning, and it is not the lamp:

*A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* (Ezekiel 36:26)

*And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.* (Ezekiel 36:27)

*But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* (Jeremiah 31:33)

The Spirit put within, and the Torah written in the heart so that a man walks in the statutes: that is oil in the vessel. Zechariah saw a lampstand that burned because oil was fed to it, and heard what the oil was:

*And said unto me, What seest thou? And I said, I have looked, and behold a candlestick all of gold, with a bowl upon the top of it, and his seven lamps thereon, and seven pipes to the seven lamps, which are upon the top thereof:* (Zechariah 4:2)

*Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of Yahuah (LORD) unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* (Zechariah 4:6)

Then the door:

*And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.* (Matthew 25:10)

*Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord), open to us.* (Matthew 25:11)

*But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.* (Matthew 25:12)

Mark who is outside. Not strangers, not the tares, but virgins who went out to meet him, with lamps, calling him *Adonai (Lord)*. They are of the house, and the door is shut on them. He had said it before, and said what the shut door is about:

*Not every one that saith unto me, Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord), shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 7:21)

*And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.* (Matthew 7:23)

Luke has the same knock and the same answer:

*When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord), open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:* (Luke 13:25)

Yahuah (the LORD) shut a door once before, on the whole earth, with the ones inside who had done as he commanded:

*And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as Elohim (God) had commanded him: and Yahuah (LORD) shut him in.* (Genesis 7:16)

The virgins outside had the lamp and the name and the right road, and no oil. The sifting at the door is of the house, the ones who called him *Adonai (Lord)* and did not walk in the statutes, and the warning is to the house:

*Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of Adam cometh.* (Matthew 25:13)

2962.prose: The ten went out with lamps to meet the bridegroom, and here is who gets in. Not the ones who only say *Adonai (Lord)*, but the one who does the will of the Father. The virgins who come knocking later call him by that same title, and it does not open the door.
2962.phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
2962.sentence: Entering the kingdom is for the one who does the Father's will, not for the one who only calls out the title.

2963.prose: A lamp can be carried by anyone. What fills the vessel is given. Yahuah (LORD) promises *a new heart* and *a new spirit* put within, with the stony heart taken out. That is the oil the wise had with their lamps and the foolish did not.
2963.phrase: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you
2963.sentence: The new heart and new spirit put within are the oil that keeps the lamp burning.

2964.prose: The covenant is made with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the virgins are of that house. What fills the vessel is Torah, *my law* put *in their inward parts* and written on the heart. Nothing is replaced. The law itself becomes what a person carries inside.
2964.phrase: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts
2964.sentence: Torah written on the heart is the oil carried inside the vessel.

2965.prose: The prophet is waked, as from sleep, to see a lampstand that keeps burning because oil is fed to it. The ten virgins carry lamps, and this is the vision that says what a lamp needs. A lamp is not its own fire. It burns on what is poured in.
2965.phrase: waked me, as a man that is wakened out of his sleep
2965.sentence: The prophet is roused to see a lampstand kept burning by oil fed to it, the picture behind the virgins' lamps.

2966.prose: Oil in the Torah is poured on what is set apart, the tabernacle *and all that was therein*. The oil goes into the vessels. The virgins went out with lamps, and the wise had the oil to go with them.
2966.phrase: Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that was therein
2966.sentence: Oil is poured on the vessels set apart to Yahuah (LORD), and the wise virgins had oil in theirs.

2967.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) is still speaking in parables, and the next one is a wedding too. The kingdom is likened to a marriage, and the ten virgins go out to meet the bridegroom. Both stories ask who gets into the wedding and who stays outside.
2967.phrase: answered and spake unto them again by parables
2967.sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) goes on speaking in parables about the kingdom and a marriage, and the virgins' story is one of them.

2968.prose: Yahuah (LORD) shut a door once before. The ones inside had done as they were commanded, and he shut them in. Everyone left outside stayed outside. The late virgins knock at a door shut the same way, on the side of those who did what he said.
2968.phrase: as Elohim (God) had commanded him: and Yahuah (LORD) shut him in
2968.sentence: Yahuah (LORD) shut the door on those who had done as commanded, the same kind of shut door the virgins meet.

2970.prose: The ten are split into wise and foolish, and this verse draws the same line. The fool is the one who despises *wisdom and instruction*. The foolish virgins took lamps and no oil. The beginning of knowledge is the fear of Yahuah (LORD), and it shows in what a person carries.
2970.phrase: but fools despise wisdom and instruction
2970.sentence: The fool is the one who despises instruction, and the foolish virgins are the ones who went out with no oil.

2971.prose: Wisdom builds a house and gets it ready, *hath hewn out* her pillars before anyone comes. The wise virgins prepared the same way, with oil in their vessels, and they were the ones who went in with the bridegroom.
2971.phrase: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars
2971.sentence: Wisdom prepares ahead, as the wise virgins did when they took oil with their lamps.

2972.prose: The foolish woman is *clamorous* and *knoweth nothing*. The foolish virgins match her: lamps, a loud cry at the door, and nothing in the vessel. Being loud is not being wise. Having the lamp is not the same as knowing him.
2972.phrase: A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, and knoweth nothing
2972.sentence: The foolish one is loud and knows nothing, like the virgins crying at the shut door.

2973.prose: What the vessel needs is offered to whoever thirsts and comes, without money. In the parable the foolish go off to buy only when the bridegroom is already on his way. What Isaiah calls everyone to take *without money and without price*, they went looking for too late.
2973.phrase: come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price
2973.sentence: The call to come and take freely is the supply the foolish virgins went looking for too late.

2974.prose: The bridegroom the virgins go out to meet is here the Lamb, and the marriage has come. His wife *hath made herself ready*, and that is what the parable asks. Those who were ready went in. Being ready is oil in the vessel, the law walked in.
2974.phrase: the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready
2974.sentence: The wife who has made herself ready is the ready virgin who goes in to the marriage.
